purpose: Determine whether the failed independent REPRO validation reflects a weak Humble validation panel or a biological mismatch between nest-level reproductive success and the previously defined colony-wide chick-production state.

fixed_comparison.panel: Exact REPRO lag-1 validation panel restricted further to colony-seasons with an available previously frozen chick-production performance state; n=61, all Humble Island.
fixed_comparison.response: The same next-year within-island relative colony growth used by the REPRO primary model.
fixed_comparison.controls: The same outcome-interval prior-size z score and colony fixed effects.
predictors_compared: REPRO mean creched chicks per monitored nest
REPRO proportion of monitored nests with at least one chick reaching creche
fixed_comparison.permutation_diagnostic: For descriptive calibration only, permute each predictor among the complete common-panel colonies within predictor season while holding response and controls fixed; 100000 draws. P-values are explicitly post hoc and cannot create a new confirmatory claim.

questions: Does the previously frozen chick-production signal remain present inside the narrow REPRO validation subset?
Does controlling for nest-level success materially reduce the chick-production coefficient?
Are the two performance measures sufficiently correlated to justify calling them the same biological state?
claim_boundaries: Do not use the post-hoc p-values as independent replication.
Do not reinterpret a significant secondary REPRO metric as rescue of the failed REPRO primary endpoint.
If chick-production remains predictive while nest-level performance does not, rename the former as a late-season colony-wide state rather than generic reproductive success.
Do not infer public-information use or individual movement from this diagnostic.
